newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia Yield Spreads-Long end gives up ground.
newsitem.headline: Australia Yield Spreads-Long end gives up ground.

text.p: Long-dated Australian bonds gave up some ground against the dollar bloc on Wednesay, partially reversing Tuesday's tightening.
The local market was outpaced by Canada, which closed strong on Tuesday in the face of a soft U.S. Treasury market on foreign buying and spread narrowing trades to the U.S.
The Canada/U.S. 30-year bond yield spread narrowed to around parity on Tuesday, an all-time low.
Canada, like other dollar bloc markets in recent days, has been benefiting from a safe-haven status for European investors amid uncertainty over EMU, analysts said.

The local market softened initially with the U.S., but yields were finishing below the days highs after two gloomy sentiment surveys for business and consumers, and outweighed an expected 12.2 percent rise in April housing finance.
The local market faces the May labour force report on Thursday, and if weak, could stir up thoughts of a further easing in monetary policy.
